text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran an AWQ vs GPTQ sweep on the new gpt-small clone, did a per-layer/channel outlier scan. Putting raw numbers and a mitigation proposal below.

kevin: paste the scan command and top offending layers?

maria: run used:```
python infra/quant/scan_outliers.py --model models/gpt-small-clone --method awq --seq 2048 --threshold 6.0 --save out/awq_scan.json
```
Raw top hits (trimmed):
```
Layer                       max_abs   pct99   outlier_ch   est_delta_acc
18.residual_proj            78.2      12.4    3            0.9
19.attn.o_proj             102.5      16.7    5            1.8
7.attn.qkv                 34.1       7.9    1            0.2
22.ffn.w2                  56.3      10.2    2            0.6
```
Note: est_delta_acc is rough from local eval of 200 prompts comparing AWQ->fp16 baseline.

sanjay: those attn.o_proj outliers make sense — output projections see big tail mass from a few channels. Did you check head granularity?

maria: yes, it's concentrated in heads 8 & 9 of layer19 — per-channel scales blow up. I tried simple clipping (by std) and saw most error come from ~top 3 channels.

kevin: thoughts: per-channel symmetric quantization for those weight rows vs full skip? per-channel gives better numeric range but AWQ's rowwise packing is heavier.

maria: agreed. My small experiment: keep most layers AWQ, but for the offending layers apply per-channel percentile scaling at 99.9 and then AWQ compress. Command:```
python infra/quant/apply_pcscale.py --model models/gpt-small-clone --layers 18,19 --percentile 99.9 --out models/gpt-small-clone-pcscale
```
Result: estimated acc delta down from 1.8 -> 0.35 on layer19, overhead ~+2% model size due to scale table.

sanjay: alternative is skip-quantize (leave FP16). On Dedicated we could map those layers to fp16 kernels and everything else AWQ — wins latency slightly but costs more memory. For on-prem customers might be better. :+1:

rain: ops note — if we start shipping mixed-quant layouts, we need a routing/fallback policy in the model manifest so Dedicated auto-fallback works. Small example snippet:```
quant_profile:
  mixed_strategy: true
  per_layer_overrides:
    - layer: 18
      strategy: fp16
    - layer: 19
      strategy: per_channel_awq
```
We should keep a cost estimate in the rollout UI.

kevin: also propose trying L2-per-channel scaling (scale by sqrt(var)+eps) before percentile clip — less brittle for noisy heads. I'll run a quick compare tomorrow.

eval-bot: automated eval (on 500 eval prompts) after per-channel-scaling + AWQ:
```
model: gpt-small-clone-pcscale-awq
PPL (mean): 18.3  (baseline fp16: 17.8)
EM@1 delta: -0.6%
avg_latency_ms: 24.1 (baseline: 22.7)
outlier_layers: [18,19]
```

maria: thanks — numbers look promising (delta within acceptable threshold). I'll prepare a short PR to add the per-layer override + manifest change, and run a larger 2k prompt eval.

kevin: if the L2-scale test helps, we can fold it into Optimize suggestions as "Apply per-channel percentile scaling for top-K outlier channels" with expected cost tradeoffs.

sanjay: tagging @rain to keep an eye on Dedicated capacity impact if we ship mixed layouts.

rain: noted. also add an annotation to the rollout that the model has "per-layer quant overrides" so console shows it.

maria: copying the minimal repro and a short notebook to the PR. Will update when 2k eval done. :rocket:
